name: 993 Turbo intercooler end tank, AlSi10Mg concept F0
description: Independent concept of a round-to-rectangular-face transition with three open internal guide vanes, used to screen an LPBF AlSi10Mg end tank. The published overall dimensions bound the F0 but define neither the core orientation nor a compatible geometry.

classification.intended_use: CAD, DfAM, flow, pressure loss, pressure, membrane, guided panel, thermal and cycle screening; no manufacture, installation or engine start-up authorized

provenance.record_license: MIT for the concept, the script and the calculations; no photograph, TA Technix/Albert/Porsche surface or commercial geometry redistributed

sources.title: TA Technix - intercooler for Porsche 911 Turbo 993
sources.notes: Publishes two 260 x 260 x 100 mm cores, 66 mm outer and 68 mm inner connections, 860 mm maximum width, 240 mm height and 690 mm center distance. The orientation and the end tanks are not defined. See SRC-TA-TECHNIX-993-INTERCOOLER-DIMENSIONS.

sources.title: Albert Motorsport - 993 Turbo/GT2 aluminum intercooler
sources.notes: Corroborates two 260 x 260 x 100 mm cores and declares a welded aluminum assembly, with no alloy and no end-tank geometry. See SRC-ALBERT-MOTORSPORT-993-ALUMINUM-INTERCOOLER.

sources.title: PorscheFanatics - 993 charge-air cooling architecture
sources.notes: Identifies the air-to-air function and the charge coolers of the 993 Turbo; no dimension or surface is transferred. See SRC-PORSCHEFANATICS-993-INTERCOOLER-END-TANK-CANDIDATE.

sources.title: EOS Aluminium AlSi10Mg material data sheet
sources.notes: Reference for a lightweight automotive LPBF material; properties and treatment remain dependent on the exact route. See SRC-EOS-ALSI10MG-CURRENT-PAGE.

sources.title: elferclassic - German technical data for the 993 Turbo
sources.notes: Publishes 3.6 l and 5,750 rpm at peak power; the screening flow, VE, boost and temperature remain synthetic. See SRC-ELFERCLASSIC-993-TURBO-TECHNICAL-DATA.

material.grade: EOS Aluminium AlSi10Mg for screening; commercial alloy unknown
material.standard: DIN EN 1706 EN AC-43000, ASTM F3318 and a program-specific end-tank specification to be contracted

post_processing: orientation and supports keeping the duct fully open for powder removal
heat treatment qualified for machine, parameters, wall and guide vanes
build plate cut-off and support removal without damaging the interfaces
machining of the core face and the connection after adding the measured machining stock
internal finishing of the guide vanes and the transition with controlled roughness
assembly to the core by qualified welding or brazing, then proof test and cleaning
supplier_requirements: traceable powder, machine, parameters, orientation, batch and recycling
capability demonstrated on a 2.2 mm wall and a 1.5 mm guide vane after post-processing
CT of the guide vanes and junctions, then metrology of the walls, face, connection and datums
oriented coupons with representative tensile, fatigue, pressure and temperature tests
comparison of LPBF, TIG-welded sheet and casting on flow, mass, cost, repairability and service life

titanium.galvanic_isolation: Qualify the AlSi10Mg interface with the aluminum core, weld/braze filler, connections, steel clamps, humidity and charge-air condensate.

known_limits: The commercial values describe the complete intercooler and define neither a core face nor an end tank.
The 260 x 100 mm interpretation, the 120 mm transition, the 2.2 mm wall and the three guide vanes are synthetic.
The 66 mm connection represents an outer position; the central 68 mm connection and the second core are not modeled.
The CAD mass of 605.92 g is that of a synthetic end tank and cannot be compared with the 14 kg of the commercial assembly.
The flow uses 3.6 l, 5,750 rpm, VE 0.95, 1.8 bar absolute, 330 K and porosity 0.65, with no measurement on the vehicle.
The 487 Pa loss is a sudden-expansion screen, not a CFD with core, turbulence or face uniformity.
The membrane/panel stresses and thermal bounds replace neither FEA, nor welding/brazing, nor pressure-temperature fatigue.
The STEP proves only an open BREP and a connected fluid volume; it is authorized neither for manufacture, nor for fitting, nor for an engine.
